prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 5 "Grub screw": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 1.10 (80% range 0.79 to 1.71); revealed per pc: 0.90-1.30 (case 40), so this line (8 pc) about 8.8 (6.3 to 13.6)
- line 7 "Two-screw pipe clamp 25 mm": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 6.2 (80% range 4.6 to 9.4); revealed per pc: >=5.7 (case 40), so this line (4 pc) about 25 (18.3 to 38)
- line 8 "Service technician hours": indemnified in all 4 earlier cases; when indemnified t per hr about 88 (80% range 72 to 104); revealed per hr: 44-49 (case 21), >=81 (case 39), >=81 (case 39), >=88 (case 40), so this line (6.75 hr) about 595 (485 to 702)
- line 9 "Helper hours": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per hr about 73 (80% range 55 to 101); revealed per hr: >=67 (case 40), so this line (5.75 hr) about 418 (316 to 581)
- line 11 "Binding wire": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per kg about 9.8 (80% range 7.2 to 15.0); revealed per kg: >=9.0 (case 40), so this line (2 kg) about 19.6 (14.5 to 30)
- line 14 "Small parts and consumables": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 36 (80% range 27 to 55); revealed per pc: >=33 (case 40)
- line 15 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 14 of 29 earlier cases, t = 0 in 15; when indemnified t per pc about 79 (80% range 72 to 87); revealed per pc: >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27), >=83 (case 34), >=76 (case 34), >=65 (case 39), >=71 (case 40)
- line 16 "Construction waste disposal": indemnified in all 2 earlier cases; when indemnified t per pc about 60 (80% range 51 to 71); revealed per pc: >=57 (case 18), 58-61 (case 40)
- line 17 "Processing flat fee": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 9 earlier cases; no price evidence

items.rationale: The failed indoor heating pipe is covered under 2.4.3(a), but 7.1.9 limits the replacement to plain copper: 6.4 m × €15 gross = €96.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow necessary equivalent fittings without the chrome premium: 4 × €10 gross = €40.
If the elbows served the repaired connections, 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 limit payment to standard fittings: 5 × €20 gross = €100.
Under 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9, the gross allowance is €20 for one standard equivalent elbow, with no chrome premium.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers ordinary repair fixings: 8 × €1.10 gross = €8.80.
The 10 mm clamps do not match the documented 15 mm pipe or 28 mm connections, so 7.1.8(e) excludes them absent a demonstrated repair use. If substantiated, 4 × €5 gross would be reasonable.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary supports for the repaired run; four clamps are estimated at €25 gross using Case 40.
Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.9 allow customary labour for an equivalent repair, not extra time for upgrades. The Case 40 benchmark for 6.75 hours is €595 gross.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary helper labour for the pipe repair, excluding work on new additions under 7.1.9. The benchmark for 5.75 hours is €418 gross.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 cap payment at the cost of the original rock-wool specification: 6 × €20 gross = €120.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers ordinary fastening material needed for reinstatement: 2 kg × €9.80 gross = €19.60.
Section 7.1.9 excludes the sensor because it was not installed before the loss. The positive figure is a conditional estimate for one unit only.
Section 7.1.9 excludes the valve because it was a new addition, not a replacement. The positive figure is a conditional estimate for one valve only.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e) allow a lump sum for minor repair consumables; the benchmark is €36 gross.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows one travel charge per contractor per invoice; the single charge is estimated at €79 gross.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover necessary disposal of the removed pipe and insulation; the benchmark is €60 gross.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes processing charges billed on top of itemised labour and materials. The positive figure is a nominal conditional estimate only.
